hypothesis: If plaice weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 peaks near maturity, k as a function of length rises to a maximum near 30 cm and declines at larger sizes.
pass_criterion: In DATRAS plaice records, the length class with maximum mean k = 100·W/L³ is between 25 and 35 cm, and k at that peak exceeds k at the smallest and largest 10% of lengths by at least 5%.
fail_criterion: The peak of k is below 20 cm or above 40 cm, or k is monotonic with length (no decline above the peak).
interpretation: k is Fulton's condition factor computed from individual weight and length. The peak is compared with the ~30 cm size at onset of maturity, which can be checked using the maturity field. Modern North Sea plaice mature at different sizes, so maturity is checked in the same data.

dataset.name: ICES DATRAS – Database of Trawl Surveys
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS survey records (CA data) have individual species, length class, individual weight and maturity stage, enabling k and maturity-at-length for plaice (Pleuronectes platessa).
